item.title: Polarization waves in open-barrier quantum-dot cellular automata
item.description:
Long shot

Grade 0.356 · 3.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation”

Abstract

Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) are almost always operated as bistable digital logic. We develop a closed-form theory of small-signal polarization waves in the open-barrier regime, where tunnelling within each cell is comparable to or stronger than the electrostatic kink coupling between cells, so that a line of cells responds linearly instead of latching. Linearizing the coherence-vector equations of the intercellular Hartree approximation (ICHA) about the unpolarized state gives a lattice dispersion with a low-frequency cutoff, an evanescent band below it and a Klein-Gordon long-wavelength limit, and relaxation toward the instantaneous equilibrium damps the waves at a rate that depends on the wavenumber. The exact Jordan-Wigner solution and exact diagonalization confirm the mode as a sharp quasiparticle, with ICHA frequencies within 6% of the exact ones once the tunnelling energy is at least twice the kink energy, and show that the exact chain also carries waves over a range of couplings where the ICHA predicts latching. A leading low-temperature estimate of thermal dephasing sets a ceiling on the operating temperature of about 13.6 K per terahertz of gap for a carrier that keeps its phase over 30 periods. At junctions the waves scatter through a lattice scattering matrix that reaches the familiar transmission-line value only at mid-band.

arxave:action.title: Check transferability to gate-defined double-dot spin qubits

item.arxave:action: The conclusion notes gate-defined double-dot chains as a gigahertz test bed. Assess whether the linear dispersion, damping and junction-scattering formalism could inform charge-noise or crosstalk characterization in the spin-qubit array, but treat this as background only unless a concrete calibration or benchmarking protocol emerges.
